use_case_name: Monitor Current and Past Auction Status

claims.content: Customer wants to monitor the current and past auction status of a product item, including its auction status (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed), dates/times, bid counts, and winning bidder information.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Customer wants to monitor the current and past auction status of a product item, including its auction status (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed), dates/times, bid counts, and winning bidder information.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Customer views one product item's current and past auction status records in the Bid History section, seeing status labels, closing date/time (or 'Active' for a live auction), auction sequence numbers, SKU, the customer's last bid, SmartBid if one was placed, and the winning bid.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Customer begins by choosing to view a product item's auction status/history.
scope_contract.success_boundary: Customer sees the product item's current and past auction status and the associated bid history details.
in_scope_actions: View current and past auction status for a product item
View auction status categories (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed) with dates/times, bid counts, and winning bidder information
View Bid History details: closing date/time or 'Active', auction sequence numbers, SKU, customer's last bid, SmartBid if placed, and winning bid
excluded_adjacent_actions: Placing, updating, or canceling bids (including QuickBid/SmartBid submission)
Managing auction scheduling or product/SKU administration
Post-auction notifications, offers, or follow-up processes
variant_dimensions: Auction status category displayed (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed)
Presence of a customer SmartBid on an auction

claims.content: Customer

The customer has an authenticated session in the customer-facing account workspace (e.g., via 'My Bid History' or 'My Account Page') and can access a product-item auction status/history view by entering a Product ID; no prior customer-history identification (email/phone/name) is required for this view.
Customer initiates the auction status view for a specific product item by entering the Product ID and clicking “Go.”
The Customer initiates the auction status/history view for a specific product item by entering the Product ID and clicking “Go.”
The system displays the search results in two sections: a top section showing product summary data and a bottom section listing the item's auction history data on separate lines.

The system lists each individual auction record with its Auction Status, Auction Sequence, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve Amount, High Bid, Number of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder. Additionally, the system displays a Bid History section showing the item's closing date/time (or 'Active' if live), auction sequence numbers, product ID (SKU) numbers, the customer's last bid, SmartBid (if placed), and the winning bid.
Diverges from Step 3: If an auction is still live, the Bid History section displays 'Active' instead of a closing date/time for that auction; if the auction is closed, its closing date/time is shown.
Diverges from Step 3: The Bid History section includes the customer's SmartBid (max bid) amount if one was placed on the auction.
Diverges from Step 2: The page provides a 'Recently Ended Auctions' link; if the customer selects it, the system displays the last 24 hours of auction history as an alternative viewing scope.

missing_aspects: Explicit confirmation that no value is displayed if no SmartBid was placed.

claims.content: If a search results in no matches (No Results Found), the system displays a 'No Results' page which includes a 'Search Tips' section with specific advice: check for typos/misspellings, remove unnecessary words like 'and', 'the', or 'a', try plural and singular forms of the word, use fewer or more generic keywords, and contact support if tips fail.

missing_aspects: Recovery/retry path after the No Results page is presented
Evidence is needed to confirm that this flow specifically occurs when a 'Product ID entry' fails at Step 1, rather than being a general outcome for any failed search.

claims.content: The system displays the specified product item's current and past auction status history in two sections: a top product summary section and a bottom section listing each auction history record on a separate line.

Each auction history record in the bottom section shows Auction Status, Auction Sequence, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve Amount (Opening Bid), High Bid, Number of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder.

The Bid History section lists each auction record with its closing date/time (or 'Active' for a live auction), auction sequence number, product ID (SKU), the customer's last bid, the SmartBid if one was placed, and the winning bid (regardless of who placed it).
The Item Bid History section lists, for each bid, the bidder's Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User? status.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Postcondition 4 requires display of an 'Item Bid History' section with per-bid fields (bidder Name, Amount, Date Placed, SmartBid User? status), but the Main Flow only describes a 'Bid History' section showing per-auction summary fields (closing date/time, auction sequence, SKU, last bid, SmartBid, winning bid). No Main Flow step leads to the per-bid Item Bid History display, so this postcondition is not reachable from the stated flow.

inconsistency_hints: The use case's primary actor is Customer, yet the preconditions describe an authenticated Auctioneer session in the Auction Admin Application and a previously identified target customer history. The trigger, however, is the Customer entering a Product ID and clicking Go. The stated preconditions therefore do not set up the Customer's Product-ID monitoring flow and instead impose an admin/customer-lookup entry context.

The main flow step 2 explicitly limits the result display to two sections (product summary and auction history records), and step 3 lists only auction-record fields. It never describes the Bid History section or the Item Bid History section required by postconditions 3 and 4, so those postconditions are not demonstrably reachable.

The trigger only requires the customer to enter a Product ID and click Go, but precondition claim 2 requires that the target customer history view already have been identified using Customer Email Address, Customer Home Phone, or Customer Name. This contradicts precondition claim 1, which explicitly says no prior customer-history identification is required, and it is not a state the trigger needs. The extra, contradictory precondition breaks the preconditions-to-trigger flow.

Main Flow step 1 names the actor as 'User', and steps 2-3 use only 'the system' as the grammatical subject. The Primary Actor 'Customer' is never explicitly named or referenced by pronoun/possessive in the main flow.

The main flow shows product summary data, auction history records, and a Bid History section, but it never displays an 'Item Bid History' section listing each bid's bidder Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User? status. Therefore postcondition 4 is not reachable from the stated main flow.
